advisor_identified: Ralph Thomas Pastore, historian and archaeologist at Memorial University of Newfoundland; supervisor of Peter E. Pope’s 1992 South Avalon planters dissertation.

doctorate.title: The Board of Commissioners for Indian Affairs in the Northern Department and the Iroquois Indians, 1775-1778

evidence.says: Canadian Historical Association prize notice, p. 17: Peter E. Pope’s South Avalon planters dissertation (History, Memorial University of Newfoundland, 1992) was completed under Professor Ralph Pastore’s supervision.

Memorial’s Gazette, 6 December 1968, p. 9, announces Ralph T. Pastore’s appointment as a history lecturer. It lists Notre Dame degrees in 1963 and 1964 and describes his doctoral research on the Continental Congress and Six Nations, 1775-78.

Notre Dame’s 21 May 1972 commencement program lists Ralph Thomas Pastore among PhD recipients (section begins p. 5; entry p. 8), with history as his subject and the dissertation title recorded above. His earlier Notre Dame degree years match Memorial’s appointment notice.
Ralph T. Pastore’s Dictionary of Canadian Biography article on Teiorhénhsere cites R. T. Pastore’s dissertation with the same title as an unpublished PhD thesis at the University of Notre Dame, 1972.

notes: The linked record matches the documented institution, year, subject and title; 1775-78 is an abbreviated form of 1775-1778. Memorial’s 1968 notice anticipated completion in 1969, but the actual conferral is documented in the 1972 commencement program. The Dictionary of Canadian Biography citation was available in indexed search text; direct retrieval returned HTTP 429.
